findings.text: follow-on: the landed guard `_has_dd_source_reference` is called only when `_bound_docs_review_dd_paths` has already returned empty, and that owner returns bare `source_paths` whenever no `dd` binding exists — so an item whose only source path is a facility entry (e.g. `tcv:ip/measured`, no dd binding) still takes the hold note 'DD source text unavailable; claim comparison could not run' although it names no DD text. That is the same false hold the node exists to remove, reached by a different trigger; the node's own manifest evidence_inputs discloses the mechanism but the brief's 'What to change' named `_bound_docs_review_dd_paths` as the DD-source test, so the implementation follows the brief as written. Does not hold the node; a follow-on node should decide whether a facility-only source counts as a DD source for this hold.

follow-on: the expected value is built from `DD_PATH`, the same module constant used to construct the input binding at line 67, so the two sides move together: an implementation that returned the path it was handed regardless of which path it was handed (or that mis-derived the path) passes as long as the tests keep using the one constant. The assertion does redden on the fallback regression it is paired with, and the independent `is None` assertions at lines 45/60 carry the node's durability, so this weakens rather than voids the guard.

follow-on: same shape as line 71 — the note's expected path is the `DD_PATH` constant that also constitutes the `source_paths` entry passed in at line 76, so the assertion cannot distinguish a correctly reported path from the constant itself; it verifies the branch is still reached (it would redden if the missing-text branch stopped holding) but not that the reported path came from the item.
